newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi households with mosquitoes face prosecution.
newsitem.headline: Delhi households with mosquitoes face prosecution.

text.p: The Indian government on Wednesday instructed authorities in the nation's capital to prosecute homeowners who failed to eradicate mosquitoes, which have caused a deadly outbreak of dengue fever.

It said in a statement that a meeting of health experts from the federal government, the city of Delhi and the Indian Red Cross Society reviewed measures to combat the outbreak, in which more than 150 people have died.
The statement said Delhi municipal authorities "were advised to launch vigorous prosecution against those who have failed to prevent mosquito breeding within their houses".
Authorities had surveyed 1.35 million households and found mosquitoes breeding in more than 55,000 of them, it said.

Mosquitoes carry the virus which causes dengue, also called breakbone fever. The disease erupted in the Indian capital in the last week of August during annual monsoon rains, and more than 3,200 victims have been admitted to local hospitals.
Earlier this week authorities called in the army to spray insecticides in mosquito-infested areas and open its hospitals to dengue patients.
The government statement said adequate amounts of blood platelets and blood plasma were available for both government and private hospitals.
Delhi authorities had eight to 10 days' worth of Pyrethrum insecticide, and more was on the way, it said.
Seven fogging machines mounted on trucks, used to spread the insecticides, were in use as well as 105 hand-operated machines.
Spraying had been completed in more than 182,000 homes, the statement said.
